C2: The GPS track contains two distinct off-route segments: 18:40-18:45 adding 3.17 km and 18:59-19:08 adding 4.78 km; each is an unexempted detour segment unless an exemption in RD-3 / RD-4 / RD-5 covers it. [F3 F4] [RD-1]
C3: For the first segment (18:40-18:45) the rider consented to a reroute in advance: the driver asked at 18:37 about going round the jam via Kranji Expressway and the rider replied at 18:38 'Sure, go ahead' - both timestamps precede the segment start of 18:40, so this segment is exempt and no refund is sought for its 3.17 km. [F8 F9 F3] [RD-5]
C4: No consent exists for the second segment: the rider's only consent message (18:38, 'Sure, go ahead') predates the second segment start of 18:59 and was given in answer to the Kranji Expressway proposal; that consent cannot extend to a separate off-route segment begun 21 minutes later and 4.78 km long (up to 1687 m off the optimal route). [F9 F8 F4] [RD-5]
C5: The driver's own written statement that 'the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting' admits he changed route on his own initiative without asking the rider, and it does not cover the second segment under RD-5. [F11 F4] [RD-5 RD-1]
C6: The driver cannot claim the second detour was justified by road conditions: no traffic incident of any kind was recorded near the route during the trip window, so RD-4(a) evidence is absent; the only band records are Better-than-severe conditions (Bukit Timah Expressway band 5, 40-49 km/h; Pan Island Expressway band 4, 30-39 km/h), which are not band 1 or 2 and cannot exempt a segment under RD-4(b).
